notes: Multicenter RCT (4 study sites) of rectal indomethacin vs placebo for post-ERCP pancreatitis (Elmunzer 2012 NEJM). Help gives no model; the trial compared treatment arms, rendered as a random intercept on site per the Census blocking rule. id is a row id whose first digit encodes the center.

formula: conc ~ biexponential two-compartment IV pharmacokinetic decay model (time); subject-specific coefficients
notes: NONLINEAR: IV indomethacin pharmacokinetics, 6 subjects, plasma concentration over time; nlme SSbiexp two-compartment model (Pinheiro & Bates 2000). Grouping Subject, time the nonlinear input.

Multicenter RCT (4 enrollment centers) of maternal periodontal treatment on pregnancy outcome (Michalowicz 2006 NEJM). Documented analysis: log-rank stratified by center and Cox proportional hazards; rendered as a linear mixed model with a center random intercept per the Census blocking rule. Gestational age censored at 37 wk, so Preg.ended...37.wk is the censoring indicator (ignored) and PID is a row id. Many baseline/visit periodontal covariates and alternate outcomes (Birthweight, Apgar) left as unused usable columns.

formula: conc ~ first-order oral absorption one-compartment pharmacokinetic model (Dose, Time); subject-specific clearance and rate constants
notes: NONLINEAR: oral theophylline pharmacokinetics, 12 subjects; nlme SSfol first-order model (Pinheiro & Bates 2000). Grouping Subject; Dose and Time are the nonlinear inputs (census Theoph rule). Wt left as an unused usable covariate.

formula: weight ~ logistic growth curve (SSlogis) in Time; chick-specific parameters, Diet as a fixed effect
notes: NONLINEAR: chick body weight over time on four protein diets; nlme logistic growth SSlogis (help seealso), Pinheiro & Bates 2000 / Crowder & Hand 1990. Grouping Chick; Time the nonlinear input, Diet a between-chick covariate.

formula: density ~ logistic assay calibration curve (SSlogis) in log(conc); run-specific parameters
notes: NONLINEAR: ELISA assay of recombinant DNase, optical density vs known concentration across assay runs; nls SSlogis fitted per run, mixed over Run (Davidian & Giltinan 1995; Pinheiro & Bates 2000). conc is the nonlinear input.

formula: conc ~ biexponential two-compartment IV pharmacokinetic decay model (time); subject-specific coefficients
notes: NONLINEAR: IV indomethacin pharmacokinetics; nlme SSbiexp two-compartment model (Pinheiro & Bates 2000). Grouping Subject, time the nonlinear input.

formula: height ~ asymptotic growth curve (SSasymp) in age; seed-source-specific parameters
notes: NONLINEAR: loblolly pine height over age by seed source; nls SSasymp (Kung 1986; Pinheiro & Bates 2000). Grouping Seed, age the nonlinear input.

formula: circumference ~ logistic growth curve (SSlogis) in age; tree-specific parameters
notes: NONLINEAR: orange tree trunk circumference over age; nls/nlme SSlogis (Pinheiro & Bates 2000). Grouping Tree, age the nonlinear input.

8x8 Latin square of honeybee repellent (lime-sulphur) potency; rowpos and colpos are the Latin-square row and column blocks, treatment (A-H) the fixed factor; rendered with row and column random intercepts per the Census blocking rule. RULE GAP: the census coordinate rule (besag.checks) sends a field layout's row/col to ignore, but here rowpos/colpos are the design's blocking factors rather than mere spatial coordinates, so they are filed as grouping factors.

formula: conc ~ first-order oral absorption one-compartment pharmacokinetic model (Dose, Time); subject-specific clearance and rate constants
notes: NONLINEAR: oral theophylline pharmacokinetics, 12 subjects; nlme SSfol first-order model (Pinheiro & Bates 2000, help example nls(conc ~ SSfol(Dose, Time, lKe, lKa, lCl))). Grouping Subject; Dose and Time are the nonlinear inputs (census Theoph rule). Wt left as an unused usable covariate.

Joyner-Boore ground-motion attenuation: peak acceleration at observation stations for 23 California earthquakes; observations repeat within event, analysed with random earthquake effects by Brillinger & Preisler (1984/85, cited). The published analysis is on log(accel) ~ log(dist); the raw columns are named. station (recording site) is a possible second crossed grouping but has many singleton levels and is left out; grouping inferred from the design, hence low.

Matched case-control of infertility after spontaneous and induced abortion; help fits conditional logistic clogit(case ~ spontaneous + induced + strata(stratum)), rendered as a random intercept on the matched set per the Census GEE/cluster rule. pooled.stratum is an alternate (pooled) matching id, ignored; age, parity and education are confounders used in an adjusted glm and left as unused usable covariates.

Michelson speed-of-light measurements, 5 experiments of 20 runs each; help frames it as a randomized block experiment with Expt the block (grouping) and Run a within-experiment index (treated as a quantitative variate here). Documented aov(Speed ~ Run + Expt) rendered with Expt as a random intercept per the Census blocking rule.

Classic randomized block design, pea yield under nitrogen/phosphate/potassium in 6 blocks; documented fixed model aov(yield ~ block + N*P*K) (Venables & Ripley, MASS). Rendered with a block random intercept per the Census blocking rule. The three-way and some two-way interactions are confounded with blocks in this design.

Student's sleep data: extra hours of sleep under two soporific drugs measured on the same 10 patients (ID); a paired design rendered as a random intercept on patient. The paired t-test in the help is the subject-random model; group is the drug.
